nodes.name: $k$-center clustering
nodes.statement: Find partition $\mathcal{C} = \{C_1, \ldots, C_k\}$ of $A$ with centers $\mathbf{c}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{c}_k$ minimizing $\Phi_{\mathrm{kcenter}}(\mathcal{C}) = \max_{j=1}^{k} \max_{\mathbf{a}_i \in C_j} d(\mathbf{a}_i, \mathbf{c}_j)$.

nodes.name: $k$-median clustering
nodes.statement: Find partition $\mathcal{C} = \{C_1, \ldots, C_k\}$ of $A$ with centers $\mathbf{c}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{c}_k$ minimizing $\Phi_{k\mathrm{median}}(\mathcal{C}) = \sum_{j=1}^{k} \sum_{\mathbf{a}_i \in C_j} d(\mathbf{a}_i, \mathbf{c}_j)$.

nodes.name: $k$-means clustering
nodes.statement: Find partition $\mathcal{C} = \{C_1, \ldots, C_k\}$ of $A$ with centers $\mathbf{c}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{c}_k$ minimizing $\Phi_{\mathrm{kmeans}}(\mathcal{C}) = \sum_{j=1}^{k} \sum_{\mathbf{a}_i \in C_j} d^2(\mathbf{a}_i, \mathbf{c}_j)$.

nodes.name: Clustering distance
nodes.statement: Distance between two $k$-clusterings $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{C}'$: $\mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{C}') = \min_{\sigma} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{k} |C_i \setminus C'_{\sigma(i)}|$, where min is over all permutations $\sigma$ of $\{1, \ldots, k\}$.

nodes.name: $(c, \epsilon)$-approximation stability
nodes.statement: A dataset satisfies $(c, \epsilon)$-approximation stability w.r.t. a given objective if every clustering $\mathcal{C}$ whose cost is within factor $c$ of minimum satisfies $\mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{C}_T) < \epsilon$.

nodes.name: Clustering standard deviation $\sigma(C)$
nodes.statement: $\sigma(C)^2 = \frac{1}{n} \max_{\mathbf{v}: |\mathbf{v}|=1} \sum_{i=1}^{n} [(\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{c}_i) \cdot \mathbf{v}]^2 = \frac{1}{n} \|A - C\|_2^2$.

nodes.name: Conductance $\Phi(S, T)$
nodes.statement: $\Phi(S, T) = \frac{\text{Number of edges from } S \text{ to } T}{\text{Total number of edges incident to } S \text{ in } G}$, measuring relative strength of similarities between disjoint vertex sets $S$ and $T$.

nodes.name: Submatrix density $d(S,T)$
nodes.statement: For matrix $A$ with nonneg. entries, subsets $S$ of rows and $T$ of columns: $d(S,T) = \frac{A(S,T)}{\sqrt{|S||T|}}$ where $A(S,T) = \sum_{i \in S, j \in T} a_{ij}$. The density $d(A) = \max_{S,T} d(S,T)$.

nodes.name: Graph Laplacian
nodes.statement: The Laplacian of a graph is $L = D - A$ where $A$ is the adjacency matrix and $D$ is the diagonal matrix of degrees. $L$ is positive semidefinite: $\mathbf{x}^T L \mathbf{x} = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{(i,j) \in E} (x_i - x_j)^2$.

nodes.name: Average cohesion $f(S)$
nodes.statement: For a set $S$ of rows of $A$, $f(S)$ is the sum of all pairwise dot products of rows in $S$ divided by $|S|$. $f(A) = \max_S f(S)$.

nodes.name: Decomposition of sum of squared distances
nodes.statement: For points $\{\mathbf{a}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{a}_n\}$ with centroid $\mathbf{c} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_i \mathbf{a}_i$: $\sum_i |\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{x}|^2 = \sum_i |\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{c}|^2 + n|\mathbf{c} - \mathbf{x}|^2$.
assumptions: $\{\mathbf{a}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{a}_n\}$ is a set of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$

nodes.statement: Expand $|\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{x}|^2 = |\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{c} + \mathbf{c} - \mathbf{x}|^2$. Cross term vanishes since $\sum_i (\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{c}) = 0$.

nodes.name: Centroid minimizes sum of squared distances
nodes.statement: For points $\{\mathbf{a}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{a}_n\}$, the sum $\sum_i |\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{x}|^2$ is minimized when $\mathbf{x}$ is the centroid $\frac{1}{n} \sum_i \mathbf{a}_i$.

nodes.name: Lloyd's algorithm ($k$-means)
nodes.statement: Start with $k$ centers. Assign each point to nearest center. Replace centers with cluster centroids. Repeat until convergence. Always converges to a local minimum of $k$-means objective.

nodes.name: Farthest Traversal $k$-clustering
nodes.statement: Pick any data point as first center. For $t = 2, \ldots, k$, pick the data point farthest from all existing centers as the $t$-th center.
output: $k$ cluster centers with radius at most $2 \times$ optimal $k$-center radius

nodes.name: Farthest Traversal 2-approximation
nodes.statement: If there is a $k$-clustering of radius $r/2$, then Farthest Traversal finds a $k$-clustering with radius at most $r$.
conclusions: Farthest Traversal finds a $k$-clustering with radius $\leq r$

nodes.statement: Suppose point $\mathbf{x}$ has distance $> r$ from all centers. Then each chosen center was also $> r$ from previous centers, giving $k+1$ points pairwise $> r$ apart. No two can share a cluster of radius $r/2$, contradicting hypothesis.
nodes.proof_strategy: contradiction via pigeonhole on $k+1$ pairwise-far points

nodes.name: Spectral projection reduces $k$-means cost
nodes.statement: Let $A_k$ be the projection of rows of $A$ to the top $k$ right singular vectors. For any rank-$\leq k$ matrix $C$: $\|A_k - C\|_F^2 \leq 8k \|A - C\|_2^2$.

Since $\mathrm{rank}(A_k - C) \leq 2k$, $\|A_k - C\|_F^2 \leq 2k \|A_k - C\|_2^2$. By triangle inequality and best rank-$k$ approximation property: $\|A_k - C\|_2 \leq \|A_k - A\|_2 + \|A - C\|_2 \leq 2\|A - C\|_2$.
nodes.proof_strategy: rank bound on Frobenius vs spectral norm + best rank-$k$ approximation

nodes.name: Spectral Clustering
nodes.statement: 1. Find top $k$ right singular vectors of $A$, project rows to get $A_k$. 2. Select random row from $A_k$, form cluster with all rows within distance $6k\sigma(C)/\varepsilon$. 3. Repeat step 2 for $k$ rounds.

nodes.name: Spectral Clustering correctness
nodes.statement: If in $k$-clustering $C$ every pair of centers is separated by $\geq 15k\sigma(C)/\varepsilon$ and every cluster has $\geq \varepsilon n$ points, then w.p. $\geq 1 - \varepsilon$, Spectral Clustering finds $C'$ differing from $C$ on $\leq \varepsilon^2 n$ points.
conclusions: W.p. $\geq 1 - \varepsilon$, output $C'$ satisfies $\mathrm{dist}(C', C) \leq \varepsilon^2 n$ misclassified points

nodes.statement: By Thm 7.4, $|M| \leq 8\varepsilon^2 n / (9k)$ points are far from their projected centers. Good points in same cluster are within $6k\sigma(C)/\varepsilon$; in different clusters $> 9k\sigma(C)/\varepsilon$ apart. Union bound over $k$ random picks shows all picks are good w.p. $\geq 1 - \varepsilon$.
nodes.proof_strategy: Markov bound on bad points via Thm 7.4 + separation argument + union bound

nodes.name: Approximation stability structural lemma
nodes.statement: Under $(c, \varepsilon)$ approx-stability for $k$-median with each cluster $\geq 2\varepsilon n$ and $\mathcal{C}_T = \mathcal{C}^*$: (1) fewer than $\varepsilon n$ points have $w_2(\mathbf{a}_i) - w(\mathbf{a}_i) \leq (c-1)w_{\mathrm{avg}}/\varepsilon$; (2) at most $5\varepsilon n/(c-1)$ points have $w(\mathbf{a}_i) \geq (c-1)w_{\mathrm{avg}}/(5\varepsilon)$.
assumptions: Each cluster in $\mathcal{C}_T$ has size $\geq 2\varepsilon n$
conclusions: Fewer than $\varepsilon n$ points have small gap $w_2 - w$
At most $5\varepsilon n/(c-1)$ points have large weight $w$

nodes.statement: Part (1): moving $\varepsilon n$ small-gap points to second-closest clusters increases cost by $\leq (c-1) \cdot OPT$, giving a $c$-approx clustering at distance $\varepsilon$ from $\mathcal{C}_T$, contradicting stability. Part (2): follows from definition of average.
nodes.proof_strategy: contradiction via constructing a near-optimal but distant clustering

nodes.name: $k$-Median Stability algorithm
nodes.statement: 1. Build graph $G$: edge $(i,j)$ if $d(\mathbf{a}_i, \mathbf{a}_j) \leq 2d_{\mathrm{crit}}$. 2. Build graph $H$: edge $(i,j)$ if they share $\geq b+1$ common neighbors in $G$, where $b = \varepsilon n + 5\varepsilon n/(c-1)$. Take $k$ largest components as $C_1, \ldots, C_k$. 3. Assign remaining points to cluster of smallest median distance.

nodes.name: Approximation Stability clustering guarantee
nodes.statement: If $A$ satisfies $(c, \varepsilon)$ approx-stability for $k$-median, each cluster in $\mathcal{C}_T$ has size $\geq \frac{10\varepsilon}{c-1}n + 2\varepsilon n + 1$, and $\mathcal{C}_T = \mathcal{C}^*$, then Algorithm $k$-Median Stability finds $\mathcal{C}$ with $\mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{C}_T) \leq \varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Single Linkage
nodes.statement: Start with each point in its own cluster. Repeatedly merge two clusters $C, C'$ with smallest $d_{\min}(C, C') = \min_{\mathbf{x} \in C, \mathbf{y} \in C'} d(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y})$ until $k$ clusters remain. Equivalent to Kruskal's MST halted at $k$ trees.

nodes.name: Single Linkage correctness
nodes.statement: If desired clustering $C_1^*, \ldots, C_k^*$ has distance $\sigma$ s.t. (1) points in different clusters are $\geq \sigma$ apart, and (2) for any cluster $C_i^*$ and any bipartition into $A, C_i^* \setminus A$, some pair across the partition has distance $< \sigma$, then single linkage recovers $C_1^*, \ldots, C_k^*$.
assumptions: Each cluster is connected at scale $< \sigma$
conclusions: Single linkage exactly recovers the target clustering

nodes.statement: Run until all cluster pairs have $d_{\min} \geq \sigma$. By (2), each $C_i^*$ is contained in one algorithm cluster. By (1) and induction, each algorithm cluster is contained in one $C_i^*$. Hence they coincide.

nodes.name: Recursive Clustering edge bound
nodes.statement: At termination of Recursive Clustering (split $W$ into $S, W \setminus S$ when $d(S) \leq \frac{1}{2}d(W)$ and $\Phi(S, W \setminus S) \leq \varepsilon$), the total number of inter-cluster edges is $\leq O(\varepsilon m \ln n)$.
conclusions: Total inter-cluster edges $\leq O(\varepsilon m \ln n)$

nodes.statement: Charge edge deletions to vertices: each $k \in S$ charged $\leq \varepsilon d(k)$ per split. Vertex is always in smaller side, so $d(W)$ halves each time, giving $\leq O(\ln n)$ charges per vertex.
nodes.proof_strategy: amortized charging argument with halving potential

nodes.name: Density vs. singular value
nodes.statement: For $n \times d$ matrix $A$ with entries in $[0,1]$: $\sigma_1(A) \geq d(A) \geq \frac{\sigma_1(A)}{4 \log n \log d}$. Subsets achieving $d(S,T) \geq \frac{\sigma_1(A)}{4 \log n \log d}$ can be found from the top singular vector.
conclusions: Dense subsets can be extracted from top singular vector

nodes.statement: Upper bound: $\sigma_1 \geq \mathbf{u}^T A \mathbf{v}$ for indicator vectors on $S, T$ gives $\sigma_1 \geq d(S,T)$. Lower bound: partition singular vector entries into $O(\log n \log d)$ dyadic blocks; each block contributes $\leq 4 d(A)$, so $\sigma_1 \leq 4 d(A) \log n \log d$.
nodes.proof_strategy: variational characterization + dyadic decomposition of singular vectors

nodes.name: Cohesion vs density and singular values
nodes.statement: $d(A)^2 \leq f(A) \leq d(A) \log n$. Also $\sigma_1(A)^2 \geq f(A) \geq c \sigma_1(A)^2 / \log n$.

nodes.name: Ward's algorithm
nodes.statement: Start with each point as its own cluster. Repeatedly merge pair $(C, C')$ minimizing $\mathrm{cost}(C \cup C') - \mathrm{cost}(C) - \mathrm{cost}(C')$ where $\mathrm{cost}(C) = \sum_{\mathbf{a}_i \in C} d^2(\mathbf{a}_i, \mathbf{c})$. Stop at $k$ clusters.

nodes.name: $k$-means on the line (dynamic programming)
nodes.statement: Sort points $a_1 \leq \ldots \leq a_n$. Use DP: for each prefix $a_1, \ldots, a_{i+1}$ and each $k' \leq k$, try all split points $j$ and combine cost of single cluster $\{a_j, \ldots, a_{i+1}\}$ with optimal $(k'-1)$-clustering of $\{a_1, \ldots, a_{j-1}\}$. Running time $O(kn^2)$.

nodes.name: Recursive Clustering via sparse cuts
nodes.statement: Start with all vertices in one cluster. If cluster $W$ has subset $S$ with $d(S) \leq \frac{1}{2}d(W)$ and $\Phi(S, W \setminus S) \leq \varepsilon$, split $W$ into $S$ and $W \setminus S$. Repeat until no such split exists.
output: Partition into clusters with no sparse internal cuts

nodes.name: Dense subgraph via network flow
nodes.statement: Build directed graph $H$: source $s$ to each edge-node (cap 1), edge-nodes to endpoint vertex-nodes (cap $\infty$), vertex-nodes to sink $t$ (cap $\lambda$). Binary search on $\lambda$. Min-cut yields densest subgraph $S$ maximizing $d(S,S) = E(S,S)/|S|$.

nodes.name: $k$-center objective
nodes.statement: $\Phi_{\mathrm{kcenter}}(\mathcal{C}) = \max_{j=1}^{k} \max_{\mathbf{a}_i \in C_j} d(\mathbf{a}_i, \mathbf{c}_j)$

nodes.name: $k$-median objective
nodes.statement: $\Phi_{k\mathrm{median}}(\mathcal{C}) = \sum_{j=1}^{k} \sum_{\mathbf{a}_i \in C_j} d(\mathbf{a}_i, \mathbf{c}_j)$

nodes.name: $k$-means objective
nodes.statement: $\Phi_{\mathrm{kmeans}}(\mathcal{C}) = \sum_{j=1}^{k} \sum_{\mathbf{a}_i \in C_j} d^2(\mathbf{a}_i, \mathbf{c}_j)$

nodes.name: Gaussian mixture density
nodes.statement: $P(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{(2\pi)^{d/2}} \frac{1}{k} \sum_{i=1}^{k} e^{-|\mathbf{x} - \mu_i|^2}$

nodes.name: Maximum likelihood as k-means
nodes.statement: $\prod_{i=1}^{n} P(\mathbf{x}^{(i)}) \approx c \cdot e^{-\sum_{i=1}^{n} |\mathbf{x}^{(i)} - \mu(\mathbf{x}^{(i)})|^2}$

nodes.name: Centroid decomposition identity
nodes.statement: $\sum_i |\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{x}|^2 = \sum_i |\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{c}|^2 + n|\mathbf{c} - \mathbf{x}|^2$

nodes.name: $k$-means as matrix Frobenius norm
nodes.statement: $\sum_{i=1}^{n} |\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{c}_i|^2 = \|A - C\|_F^2$

nodes.name: Bad points bound from Thm 7.4
nodes.statement: $|M| \cdot 9k^2 \sigma^2(C)/\varepsilon^2 \leq \|A_k - C\|_F^2 \leq 8kn\sigma^2(C)$ implies $|M| \leq 8\varepsilon^2 n/(9k)$

nodes.name: Standard deviation of clustering
nodes.statement: $\sigma(C)^2 = \frac{1}{n} \max_{\mathbf{v}: |\mathbf{v}|=1} |(A - C)\mathbf{v}|^2 = \frac{1}{n} \|A - C\|_2^2$

nodes.name: Laplacian quadratic form
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{x}^T L \mathbf{x} = \sum_i d_{ii} x_i^2 - \sum_{(i,j) \in E} x_i x_j = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{(i,j) \in E} (x_i - x_j)^2$

nodes.name: Stochastic block model inter-centroid distance
nodes.statement: $|\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{v}|^2 \approx (\alpha - \beta)^2/n$, so inter-centroid distance $\approx (\alpha - \beta)/\sqrt{n}$

nodes.name: Clustering distance formula
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{C}') = \min_{\sigma} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{k} |C_i \setminus C'_{\sigma(i)}|$

nodes.name: Critical distance in stability algorithm
nodes.statement: $d_{\mathrm{crit}} = (c-1) w_{\mathrm{avg}} / (5\varepsilon)$

nodes.name: Conductance definition
nodes.statement: $\Phi(S, T) = \frac{\text{edges from } S \text{ to } T}{\text{total edges incident to } S}$

nodes.name: Density definition
nodes.statement: $d(S,T) = A(S,T) / \sqrt{|S||T|}$ where $A(S,T) = \sum_{i \in S, j \in T} a_{ij}$

nodes.name: Variational characterization for density bound
nodes.statement: $\sigma_1(A) \geq \mathbf{u}^T A \mathbf{v} = d(S,T) = d(A)$ for indicator vectors $\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v}$

nodes.name: Dyadic block bound
nodes.statement: $\sum_{\alpha \leq x_i \leq 2\alpha} \sum_{\beta \leq y_j \leq 2\beta} x_i y_j a_{ij} \leq 4 \alpha \beta A(S,T) \leq 4 d(A)$

nodes.name: Kernel distance formula
nodes.statement: $|\phi(\mathbf{x}) - \phi(\mathbf{y})|^2 = K(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}) + K(\mathbf{y},\mathbf{y}) - 2K(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$

nodes.name: Gaussian kernel
nodes.statement: $K(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) = e^{-\|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\|^2 / (2\sigma^2)}$

nodes.name: Flow cut capacity
nodes.statement: Cut capacity $= e - e_s + \lambda v_s$ where $e_s, v_s$ are edges and vertices of subgraph

nodes.name: Expand squared distance around centroid
nodes.statement: $|\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{x}|^2 = |\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{c} + \mathbf{c} - \mathbf{x}|^2 = |\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{c}|^2 + 2(\mathbf{c} - \mathbf{x}) \cdot (\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{c}) + |\mathbf{c} - \mathbf{x}|^2$.

nodes.name: Cross term vanishes
nodes.statement: Summing over $i$: the cross term becomes $2(\mathbf{c} - \mathbf{x}) \cdot \sum_i (\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{c}) = 0$ since $\mathbf{c}$ is the centroid.

nodes.name: Obtain decomposition
nodes.statement: Therefore $\sum_i |\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{x}|^2 = \sum_i |\mathbf{a}_i - \mathbf{c}|^2 + n|\mathbf{c} - \mathbf{x}|^2$.

nodes.name: Assume for contradiction a far point exists
nodes.statement: Suppose data point $\mathbf{x}$ has distance $> r$ from all $k$ chosen centers.

nodes.name: Each center was also far from previous centers
nodes.statement: Since the algorithm picks farthest points, each new center was distance $> r$ from all previous centers (otherwise $\mathbf{x}$ would have been chosen instead).

nodes.name: k+1 pairwise-far points contradict hypothesis
nodes.statement: The $k$ centers plus $\mathbf{x}$ give $k+1$ points pairwise $> r$ apart. No two can share a cluster of radius $r/2$ (by triangle inequality), so $k+1$ clusters are needed, contradicting the existence of a $k$-clustering of radius $r/2$.

nodes.name: Rank bound gives Frobenius-spectral relation
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{rank}(A_k - C) \leq \mathrm{rank}(A_k) + \mathrm{rank}(C) \leq 2k$, so $\|A_k - C\|_F^2 \leq 2k \|A_k - C\|_2^2$.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality plus best rank-k approximation
nodes.statement: $\|A_k - C\|_2 \leq \|A_k - A\|_2 + \|A - C\|_2$. Since $A_k$ is the best rank-$k$ approximation in spectral norm and $C$ has rank $\leq k$: $\|A_k - A\|_2 \leq \|A - C\|_2$. So $\|A_k - C\|_2 \leq 2\|A - C\|_2$.

nodes.name: Define bad points M and bound |M|
nodes.statement: Let $M = \{i : |\mathbf{v}_i - \mathbf{c}_i| \geq 3k\sigma(C)/\varepsilon\}$. Then $|M| \cdot 9k^2\sigma^2(C)/\varepsilon^2 \leq \|A_k - C\|_F^2 \leq 8kn\sigma^2(C)$ by Thm 7.4, so $|M| \leq 8\varepsilon^2 n/(9k)$.

nodes.name: Good points separated by cluster membership
nodes.statement: Good points ($i \notin M$) in same cluster: projections within $6k\sigma(C)/\varepsilon$. Good points in different clusters: projections $> 15k\sigma(C)/\varepsilon - 6k\sigma(C)/\varepsilon = 9k\sigma(C)/\varepsilon$ apart.

nodes.name: Union bound on random picks
nodes.statement: Prob first pick is bad: $\leq |M|/n \leq \varepsilon^2/k$. Each subsequent pick: $\leq \varepsilon/k$ bad since $\geq (\varepsilon - \varepsilon^2)n$ good points remain. Union over $k$ picks: failure prob $\leq \varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Part 1: construct distant clustering
nodes.statement: If $\varepsilon n$ points have gap $w_2 - w \leq (c-1)w_{\mathrm{avg}}/\varepsilon$, move them to second-closest clusters. Cost increase $\leq \varepsilon n \cdot (c-1)w_{\mathrm{avg}}/\varepsilon = (c-1) \cdot OPT$, so new clustering has cost $\leq c \cdot OPT$.

nodes.name: Part 1: contradiction with stability
nodes.statement: The new clustering $\mathcal{C}'$ has $\mathrm{dist}(\mathcal{C}', \mathcal{C}_T) = \varepsilon$ (moved $\varepsilon n$ points, each cluster has $\geq 2\varepsilon n$ so permutation remains identity). This contradicts $(c,\varepsilon)$-stability.

nodes.name: Part 2: Markov on weights
nodes.statement: If more than $5\varepsilon n/(c-1)$ points had $w(\mathbf{a}_i) \geq (c-1)w_{\mathrm{avg}}/(5\varepsilon)$, then $\sum w(\mathbf{a}_i) > n \cdot w_{\mathrm{avg}} = OPT$, contradiction.

nodes.name: Run until pairs have d_min >= sigma
nodes.statement: Run single linkage until all remaining cluster pairs satisfy $d_{\min}(C, C') \geq \sigma$.

nodes.name: Each target cluster contained in one algorithm cluster
nodes.statement: By condition (2), for any bipartition of $C_i^*$, some pair across the partition has distance $< \sigma$. So all points of $C_i^*$ must have been merged into the same algorithm cluster.

nodes.name: Each algorithm cluster contained in one target cluster
nodes.statement: By condition (1), any merger across different target clusters requires $d_{\min} \geq \sigma$. By induction, no such merger has occurred, so each algorithm cluster is within a single $C_i^*$.

nodes.name: Charge edge deletions to vertices in S
nodes.statement: When splitting $W$ into $S$ and $W \setminus S$ with $\Phi(S, W \setminus S) \leq \varepsilon$, each vertex $k \in S$ is charged at most $\varepsilon d(k)$ (its share of deleted edges).

nodes.name: Vertex always in smaller side
nodes.statement: Since $d(S) \leq d(W)/2$, vertex $k$ is always in the smaller side when charged. So $d(W)$ for $k$'s cluster halves between consecutive charges.

nodes.name: Logarithmic bound on charges per vertex
nodes.statement: Since $d(W)$ halves each time, vertex $k$ is charged at most $\log_2 m \leq O(\ln n)$ times. Total charge: $\sum_k \varepsilon d(k) \cdot O(\ln n) = O(\varepsilon m \ln n)$.

nodes.name: Upper bound: sigma_1 >= d(A)
nodes.statement: For $S,T$ achieving $d(A)$, set $\mathbf{u} = \mathbf{1}_S/\sqrt{|S|}$ and $\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{1}_T/\sqrt{|T|}$. Then $\sigma_1(A) \geq \mathbf{u}^T A \mathbf{v} = A(S,T)/\sqrt{|S||T|} = d(S,T) = d(A)$.

nodes.name: Partition singular vectors into dyadic blocks
nodes.statement: Write $\sigma_1 = \sum_{i,j} x_i a_{ij} y_j$. Ignore entries $x_i < 1/(2\sqrt{n})$ and $y_j < 1/(2\sqrt{d})$ at cost $\leq \sigma_1/4$. Group remaining into $O(\log n \cdot \log d)$ dyadic blocks.

nodes.name: Each block contributes at most 4d(A)
nodes.statement: For block with $\alpha \leq x_i < 2\alpha$ and $\beta \leq y_j < 2\beta$: $|S| \leq 1/\alpha^2$, $|T| \leq 1/\beta^2$. Contribution $\leq 4\alpha\beta A(S,T) \leq 4\alpha\beta d(S,T)\sqrt{|S||T|} \leq 4 d(A)$.

nodes.name: Sum over blocks gives lower bound
nodes.statement: $\sigma_1 \leq \sigma_1/4 + 4 d(A) \cdot O(\log n \log d)$, so $d(A) \geq \sigma_1/(4 \log n \log d)$.

edges.note: setting x = c zeros the second term
centroid update step justified by Corollary 7.2
DP optimizes k-means on the line
bounds number of bad points after projection
relates cohesion to density and singular values
Laplacian variant used for k=2 spectral clustering
critical distance derived from structural lemma
